Updated read using the February 2022 Beige Book as context:
- The FOMC’s 25 bp liftoff, guidance for ongoing hikes, and coming balance sheet reduction reflect elevated, broad-based inflation—consistent with Beige Book reports of widespread price increases and strong wage growth across districts.
- Beige Book corroborates tight labor markets and strong labor demand alongside worker shortages and Omicron-related absenteeism (notably in New York), which aligns with the statement’s “job gains strong” but acknowledges near-term frictions.
- Activity remained modest-to-moderate overall with manufacturing continuing to grow, offset by pandemic-related disruptions and supply constraints; this tempers the growth-negative tilt from Ukraine-related uncertainty.
- SLOOS suggests business credit conditions are still supportive (eased standards, strong C&I/CRE demand), which partially cushions growth. On the household side, Beige Book evidence of ongoing demand contrasts with SLOOS signs of cooling in housing/consumer credit, implying emerging headwinds as rates rise.

Net tone: hawkish policy stance with elevated inflation and downside growth risks, but Beige Book’s continued expansion, tight labor markets, and supportive business credit make the outlook slightly less negative than an FSR-only or rates-only read.
